TODAY IN NAVAL HISTORY

1862

Monitor, the Union’s first ironclad vessel, is launched at Greenpoint, New York. It is a timely appearance for the revolutionary ship, as the Confederate ironclad Virginia (ex-Merrimack) is nearing completion at Norfolk, Virginia.

1944

CDR John Tennent, III, USNA '32, USN was killed in action when USS Anderson (DD 411) was struck by artillery fire from Wotje Atoll in the Marshall Islands chain. He had been the ship's commanding officer since May 1943. As commanding officer of a previous ship, USS Southard (DD 207), he was awarded the Navy Cross for destroying a Japanese submarine after prosecuting the attack for over eight hours. He was posthumously awarded the Legion of Merit. John was survived by his wife and mother; his father was a Navy Captain who predeRUd him.

1945

Task Groups 78.3 (Rear Admiral Arthur D. Struble, USN (USNA 1915) and 78.2 (Rear Admiral William M. Fechteler, USN (USNA 1916) land Army troops in Subic Bay and Manila Bay, Philippines, in an effort to outflank the Japanese forces defending the Philippine capital. (30–31 January)

1952

VADM Lynde D. McCormick, USNA '15, USN (Ret.) is named the North Atlantic Treaty Organization's (NATO) first Supreme Allied Commander Atlantic. The command becomes operational on 10 April.

1968

Though in previous years an informal truce has been observed during Tet, the Vietnamese New Year, on this day the North Vietnamese launch a massive offensive throughout South Vietnam. The Tet Offensive results in some 32,000 enemy casualties, but succeeds in turning American public opinion against the war.

The end.
